bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regional volume concentration — The SWOT weakness disclosure states around 86% of volume has been constricted to two locations, Banaskantha and Fatehgarh Sahib, even with operational capacity spread over four zones - a structural concentration exposure that the Company expects to mitigate only as sales volumes rise in the Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli and Diu & Gir Somnath GAs.
- Gas supply volatility and sourcing dependence — Operational dependency on APM gas and imported LNG creates sourcing and pricing challenges. The CEO's message notes APM allocation to the CGD sector stood at around 30.80% in March 2026 and is slowly reducing to around 20%, adding pressure on cost dynamics. The supply chain risk row adds that dependence on a limited number of upstream gas suppliers could lead to supply disruptions or pricing pressures; mitigation is via medium- and long-term gas contracts, wider supplier relationships and exchange-based procurement.
- Regulatory risk — Changes in government policies, gas pricing frameworks or environmental regulations may affect operations and profitability. The business runs entirely under PNGRB authorisations, so regulatory change is structural rather than incidental; mitigation is active engagement with regulators and ongoing compliance readiness.
- Input gas price volatility compressing margins — Fluctuations in input gas costs present an ongoing challenge to margin stability, listed as a SWOT threat and echoed in the macroeconomic risk row (crude oil prices, inflation, interest rates and economic slowdowns may impact demand and margins). The Company proactively rationalises selling price to mitigate this.
- Infrastructure execution risk - project delays and cost overruns — Delays or cost overruns in pipeline and CGD network expansion may affect rollout timelines and returns. Unforeseen delays in land acquisition, environmental permits and regulatory clearances can hold up pipelines and CNG stations. Mitigation is strong project oversight, regular monitoring, performance-linked contractor agreements and fixed-rate contracts.
- Competitive risk from new CGD entrants and alternative fuels — New CGD entrants and alternative fuel technologies such as EVs and hydrogen could impact market share and growth prospects. Mitigation is strengthening position within existing GAs, accelerating network expansion, driving CNG and PNG conversion, partnering with OEMs and exploring LNG and EV-related opportunities.
- Strategic risk in newer, less mature geographical areas — As IRM Energy expands into newer and less mature GAs, it faces slower-than-anticipated customer addition, infrastructure deployment delays and lower-than-projected volume offtake. The Company addresses this through disciplined project tracking, return-focused capital deployment and phased infrastructure rollout.
- Supplier and channel concentration — BRSR openness-of-business disclosures show 100% of purchases are made from trading houses, with the top 10 trading houses accounting for 100% of those purchases, and sales to dealers/distributors at 59.65% of total sales in FY2025-26 - concentration exposures on both the sourcing and distribution sides.

outlook.body: FY26 was defined by the pace and scale of infrastructure development. The Company commissioned 39 new CNG stations during the year, taking the network to a landmark 150 CNG stations as of March 31, 2026 (up from 111 in FY25), supported by 552 dispensing points; capacity enhancement and upgradation activities were also carried out at 2 existing CNG stations, lifting total compression capacity to 26 lakh SCM per day, enough to cater to approximately 2.3 lakh vehicles daily. The pipeline network expanded to over 6,695 inch-km of steel and MDPE pipelines (3,172 km), with approximately 34 km of steel pipeline and more than 383 km of MDPE network added during the year; the 828-metre HDD crossing of the Banas River was the longest HDD executed by IRM Energy and an engineering milestone for the Banaskantha pipeline project. The Company also progressed CGS connectivity in the Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli and Diu & Gir Somnath GAs and executed a hook-up agreement with GSPL Transmission Limited. A first LNG dispensing facility was commissioned at the LCNG station at Rasipuram in the Namakkal-Trichy corridor, diversifying the fuel offering beyond CNG. Cumulative capital expenditure crossed Rs 1,000 crore as of March 31, 2026, with additional capex of Rs 184.57 crore deployed during FY26 (per the CEO's message). On renewables, a 3.123 MW DC captive solar plant was commissioned and operationalised, offsetting electricity consumption at 23 CNG stations in Banaskantha GA and generating approximately 47 lakh kWh; captive solar projects of 3.25 MW DC in Banaskantha GA and 0.71 MW DC in Diu & Gir-Somnath GA are in implementation and targeted for commissioning in FY2026-27, expected to benefit 65 CNG stations and generate approximately 65 lakh kWh annually, backed by planned investment of approximately Rs 13.21 crore in FY2026-27. The Company also deployed 25 additional BS-VI compliant CNG HCVs and 9 additional Type-III composite mobile cascades, taking total cascade deployment to 70.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Natural gas currently accounts for only around 6% of India's energy mix against a Government target of 15% by 2030, leaving considerable headroom for growth and creating strong structural opportunity for CGD operators
- Indian natural gas consumption is forecast to grow by nearly 60% by 2030, reaching 71,314 MMSCM, driven by rapid CGD network expansion, rising industrial demand and increasing use in power generation
- Government policy support - expansion of PNG access, the National PNG Drive, promotion of cleaner fuels, strengthening of gas infrastructure and facilitation of LPG-to-PNG transition - continues to support development of the natural gas ecosystem and lets CGD companies deepen penetration across households, institutions, commercial establishments and transportation
- Government infrastructure plans include expanding the natural gas pipeline network by 10,805 km, commissioning Compressed Bio-Gas plants and growing refining capacity, with CGD expansion a key pillar of that strategy
- A US$ 67 billion strategic gas sector investment plan with planned sector investments of up to Rs 35 lakh crore by 2035 is driving large-scale infrastructure development across the value chain
- PNGRB has established formal guidelines standardising safe injection of Compressed Bio-Gas into existing city gas pipelines, and Rs 497.25 crore has been allocated to develop CBG pipeline injection infrastructure - opening a sourcing diversification opportunity
- Reduction in APM gas allocation to the CGD sector, at around 30.80% in March 2026 and slowly reducing to around 20%, has added pressure on cost dynamics and reinforces the importance of efficient gas sourcing and portfolio optimisation
- High cost of imported LNG remains a key constraint on natural gas competitiveness against cheaper coal, and infrastructure development has not kept pace with potential demand, creating bottlenecks in transportation, small industries, commercial applications and refining
- Rupee depreciation against the US Dollar and volatility in global energy prices during FY26 reinforced the importance of agile sourcing and financial discipline for an energy company
- Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli continues to emerge as the fastest-growing GA with significant headroom as infrastructure rollout accelerates, while Banaskantha, Fatehgarh Sahib and Diu & Gir Somnath saw continued network densification and steady customer additions
- Volume growth momentum was broad-based in FY26 - 116.8% YoY in Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli, 25.4% in Diu & Gir Somnath and 16.2% in Banaskantha

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Natural gas currently accounts for only around 6% of India's energy mix against a Government target of 15% by 2030, leaving considerable headroom for growth and creating strong structural opportunity for CGD operators
- Indian natural gas consumption is forecast to grow by nearly 60% by 2030, reaching 71,314 MMSCM, driven by rapid CGD network expansion, rising industrial demand and increasing use in power generation
- Government policy support - expansion of PNG access, the National PNG Drive, promotion of cleaner fuels, strengthening of gas infrastructure and facilitation of LPG-to-PNG transition - continues to support development of the natural gas ecosystem and lets CGD companies deepen penetration across households, institutions, commercial establishments and transportation
- Government infrastructure plans include expanding the natural gas pipeline network by 10,805 km, commissioning Compressed Bio-Gas plants and growing refining capacity, with CGD expansion a key pillar of that strategy
- A US$ 67 billion strategic gas sector investment plan with planned sector investments of up to Rs 35 lakh crore by 2035 is driving large-scale infrastructure development across the value chain
- PNGRB has established formal guidelines standardising safe injection of Compressed Bio-Gas into existing city gas pipelines, and Rs 497.25 crore has been allocated to develop CBG pipeline injection infrastructure - opening a sourcing diversification opportunity
- Reduction in APM gas allocation to the CGD sector, at around 30.80% in March 2026 and slowly reducing to around 20%, has added pressure on cost dynamics and reinforces the importance of efficient gas sourcing and portfolio optimisation
- High cost of imported LNG remains a key constraint on natural gas competitiveness against cheaper coal, and infrastructure development has not kept pace with potential demand, creating bottlenecks in transportation, small industries, commercial applications and refining
- Rupee depreciation against the US Dollar and volatility in global energy prices during FY26 reinforced the importance of agile sourcing and financial discipline for an energy company
- Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli continues to emerge as the fastest-growing GA with significant headroom as infrastructure rollout accelerates, while Banaskantha, Fatehgarh Sahib and Diu & Gir Somnath saw continued network densification and steady customer additions
- Volume growth momentum was broad-based in FY26 - 116.8% YoY in Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli, 25.4% in Diu & Gir Somnath and 16.2% in Banaskantha
- Institutional and fleet conversion demand is building - CNG supply commenced to 71 TNSTC buses in Namakkal and an MoU with Red Taxi in Trichy converted 120 taxis to CNG

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was defined by the pace and scale of infrastructure development. The Company commissioned 39 new CNG stations during the year, taking the network to a landmark 150 CNG stations as of March 31, 2026 (up from 111 in FY25), supported by 552 dispensing points; capacity enhancement and upgradation activities were also carried out at 2 existing CNG stations, lifting total compression capacity to 26 lakh SCM per day, enough to cater to approximately 2.3 lakh vehicles daily. The pipeline network expanded to over 6,695 inch-km of steel and MDPE pipelines (3,172 km), with approximately 34 km of steel pipeline and more than 383 km of MDPE network added during the year; the 828-metre HDD crossing of the Banas River was the longest HDD executed by IRM Energy and an engineering milestone for the Banaskantha pipeline project. The Company also progressed CGS connectivity in the Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli and Diu & Gir Somnath GAs and executed a hook-up agreement with GSPL Transmission Limited. A first LNG dispensing facility was commissioned at the LCNG station at Rasipuram in the Namakkal-Trichy corridor, diversifying the fuel offering beyond CNG. Cumulative capital expenditure crossed Rs 1,000 crore as of March 31, 2026, with additional capex of Rs 184.57 crore deployed during FY26 (per the CEO's message). On renewables, a 3.123 MW DC captive solar plant was commissioned and operationalised, offsetting electricity consumption at 23 CNG stations in Banaskantha GA and generating approximately 47 lakh kWh; captive solar projects of 3.25 MW DC in Banaskantha GA and 0.71 MW DC in Diu & Gir-Somnath GA are in implementation and targeted for commissioning in FY2026-27, expected to benefit 65 CNG stations and generate approximately 65 lakh kWh annually, backed by planned investment of approximately Rs 13.21 crore in FY2026-27. The Company also deployed 25 additional BS-VI compliant CNG HCVs and 9 additional Type-III composite mobile cascades, taking total cascade deployment to 70.

Per-segment growth: CNG / PNG-commercial / PNG-industrial each "more than 20% YoY"; industrial to catch up to 23-24% if NGT order implemented.
- **EBITDA/scm:** target **INR 5.3–5.5/scm** (from >INR 5.0); +10-15% improvement guided. Gross margin held at 25-26%.
- **Capex FY27:** Namakkal & Trichy alone INR 150 cr (internal target INR 170-180 cr). Funded by IPO funds (INR 194 cr available at Mar-end) for N&T; other 3 GAs via internal accruals + INR 40-45 cr term-loan line.
- **CNG station adds FY27:** ~36 new stations (vs 39 added in FY26).
- **Peak debt:** INR 70-80 cr range for FY27 (term loans ~INR 49 cr at Mar-end + INR 45 cr sanctioned).
volume / pipeline:
- FY26 total volume 223.67 MMSCM (+9%). GA split (mgmt, volume basis): Banaskantha ~47%, Fatehgarh Sahib ~39%, balance DGS + Namakkal-Trichy.
- Pipeline network 6,695 inch-km. PNG connections: 83,262 domestic adds, 496 commercial, 223 industrial across 4 GAs in FY26.
- Banaskantha: 63,588 metered residential, 300+ commercial, 15+ industrial, 65 CNG stations. DGS crossed 10,000 domestic PNG. Namakkal-Trichy: 49 CNG stations, daily CNG demand ~doubled (100% jump) YoY.
segment (cng / industrial / domestic):
- **CNG:** ~61% of total operational revenue; most profitable (margin & net-margin) segment; ~75-80% of CNG sourcing from domestic gas. New 3-wheeler sales ~92-95% CNG in Namakkal-Trichy; Banaskantha passenger-vehicle CNG penetration >40%, N&T >15% and rising. Spot purchases only ~4% of full-year CNG.
- **Industrial PNG:** concentrated in Fatehgarh Sahib (industrial zone); hit by DCQ cuts and demand destruction from higher prices; Banaskantha industrial +13% YoY; awaiting NGT order implementation to lift volumes off low base.
- **Domestic/commercial PNG:** strong adds; rising LPG-substitution demand (LPG shortage driving conversions in hotels/commercial); PNGRB mandate caps domestic coverage at ~1/3 of population.
growth / optionality:
- **New GA ramp:** Namakkal & Trichy is the flagship growth GA — INR 257 cr gross block to date, +INR 150-180 cr FY27 capex; 4-5 national/state highways pass through (mobility potential). MoU with TNSTC for PNG/CNG buses (71 running, +50 in May, ~6,000 kg/day, 17% of N&T CNG volume); Red Taxi Trichy MoU (120+ taxis converted); Trichy bus-stand CNG station planned.
- **LNG/LCNG:** first LNG dispensing facility commissioned at Rasipuram (N&T); agreement with Ultra Gas Trading; lining up transporter hubs.
- **CBG/biogas:** tripartite IRM-GAIL-CBG-producer agreements across all 4 GAs under GAIL CBG-CGD Synchronization Scheme; Farm Gas (33% JV) supplying CBG from Khanna plant — "very profitable currently" amid gas shortage.
- **Backward integration:** Venuka Polymers (50% JV) — MDP P80/P100 pipes + irrigation + power-conduit; turnover expected to ~double / 2.5x next year.
- **Other:** Grasim Industries (DGS) & District Jail (BK) PNG MoUs for residential colonies; GreenMile+ fleet cards (Zaggle partnership).
margins & cost (apm cut → high-cost gas;:
- **APM allocation CUT in Q4** + ceiling price $6.75→$7.00/MMBTU; NWG formula prices up — the core cost pressure. Fully passed through to CNG/industrial/commercial customers from April; "margins intact."
- HPHT price decline ($9.72→$8.92) and ~75-80% domestic sourcing for CNG cushion the cost. CGD enjoys priority-sector gas allocation, so domestic/mobility largely insulated vs industrial/power/fertilizer.
- **EV competition:** mgmt downplays — EV penetration "negligible" across GAs; only "some extent" a threat in Tamil Nadu (N&T). 3-wheeler EV conversion is "a debate." CNG vehicle additions still growing per Vahan data.
- Cost levers: type-3 cascades (~35% of fleet) and online stations to cut OpEx/scm; license fee 2% of net revenue; OpEx/scm to fall as volumes rise.
capex:
- FY26 capex INR 184.35 cr (Q4 INR 81.33 cr). FY27 guide: N&T INR 150-180 cr (IPO funds); other GAs internal accruals + bank line. Cumulative gross block: Banaskantha ~INR 420 cr, Fatehgarh Sahib ~INR 200 cr, N&T INR 257 cr.
- Station model: DODO and OMC (where DODO not viable), COCO where cheap land available; preference for online stations over daughter-booster.
capital allocation: - Net cash +INR 170 cr; debt-light (INR 72 cr total incl. leases, down from INR 140 cr). Expansion funded largely via internal accruals + IPO proceeds (INR 194 cr unutilised). Disciplined IRR/return-based allocation. Board-approved treasury policy parks surplus in liquid/overnight funds (~INR 700 cr rotation; other income ~INR 2 cr/qtr, INR 68 lakh in Q4). No dividend mentioned.
risks:
- **APM gas allocation cuts** + rising ceiling/NWG prices → high-cost gas (mitigant: pass-through, HPHT, domestic sourcing, priority allocation).
- **Gas-sourcing/geopolitical:** Gulf war disrupted LNG; force-majeure invoked (restricted to industrial). Long-term contracts (Shell/GSPC, portfolio-based not Qatar-specific) provide insulation.
- **Industrial demand destruction** in Fatehgarh Sahib (DCQ cuts, higher prices, AAP-era de-growth); NGT order implementation deferred to avoid agitating customers.
- **EV/CNG price-competitiveness** (mainly Tamil Nadu); late-licensed high-capex GA economics take time to match incumbents (IGL/MGL).
- JV receivable recoverability (Ni Hon); execution risk on aggressive N&T rollout / new TN government policy.
mgmt tone: Confident and candid, but explicitly cautious on hard guidance given "evolving" geopolitical/sourcing situation ("giving a predictable guidance is a challenge... I hope my investors will pardon me"). Repeatedly stresses margin protection via pass-through and net-cash discipline. Proud of 150-station landmark and accident-free year. Transparent on Q4 one-offs and willingness to walk through P&L line items with investors.
non-obvious:
- ~40% of CNG volume tied to NWG/APM; APM cut offset by NWG — sourcing mix is the real margin driver, not headline price.
- HPHT gas (IGX, prorated allocation) is the competitive swing source and got CHEAPER in Q4, a hidden tailwind.
- Late-licensed CGDs structurally disadvantaged on capex intensity & sourcing scale vs IGL/MGL, but win on private-sector operational efficiency.
- Shizuoka Gas (Japan shareholder) provides essentially no sourcing/technical benefit — min LNG ship size (~40,000 units) too large.
- Treasury earns meaningful float income via daily dealer-proceed collection by 1 pm parked in overnight funds.
- New labour code forced ~INR 60 lakh extra provisioning (industry-wide Q4 effect).
qoq log: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** FY26 — Rev INR 1,066.66 cr (+9%), EBITDA INR 112.25 cr (+17%), PAT INR 56.89 cr (+21%), Volume 223.67 MMSCM (+9%), Net cash +INR 170 cr, 150 CNG stations (+39). Q4 PAT ~INR 13 cr (vs Q3 ~INR 15 cr) hit by 2 one-offs (INR 1.34 cr JV provision + INR 2.86 cr bank charge, both reversing Q1 FY27). APM allocation cut + ceiling $6.75→$7.00; NWG up; HPHT down $9.72→$8.92. FY27 guide: volume >250 MMSCM (double-digit / 30%+ on segments), EBITDA/scm INR 5.3-5.5, ~36 station adds, N&T capex INR 150-180 cr.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
